plan: With a private value of $25, I want to maximize potential profit. Since values are uniformly distributed between $0-$49, rational bidders will likely bid strategically around their private values. My optimal strategy is to bid slightly above my value but not so high that I risk negative earnings. I'll aim to bid around $30 - high enough to increase win probability but not so high that I risk overpaying if my value is only $25.

In a first-price sealed bid auction with values drawn from $0-$49, a rational strategy is to bid slightly below my true value. Since my value is $17, I want to maximize potential profit. Other bidders likely have random values between $0-$49. I'll bid strategically to increase my chances of winning while minimizing overpayment. A bid around $15-$16 seems optimal - low enough to potentially win, but not risking paying more than the item's worth to me.

With a private value of $39, I want to maximize potential profit. Since values are randomly drawn between $0-$49, rational bidders will likely bid strategically near their value. My optimal strategy is to bid slightly below my true value to minimize overpaying. Given the third-price auction mechanism, I'll bid around $35 - this gives me room to potentially win while protecting against significant loss if my value is higher than competitors.
